conventions.convention: Spacetime is Newtonian I × E with absolute time. A frame is an adapted Cartesian chart. Inertial changes have constant proper rotation and affine spatial translation; general rigid observer changes may have time-dependent proper rotation.
Material motions are jointly C2 orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms on a neighborhood of the closed reference body, with J > 0. The initial-chart convention requires 0 ∈ I and χ(0,a) = a.
Lij = ∂j ui, D = (L + Lᵀ)/2, θ = div u, and D0 = D − θI3/3. Stress is tension-positive, traction is σn, tensor divergence is rowwise, and objective tensor responses transform as S* = QSQᵀ.
Material incompressibility means div u = 0; spatially homogeneous density means ∇ρ = 0. Pathlines use the time-dependent velocity, whereas streamlines use a frozen-time velocity.

Volume integrals use Riemann zero extensions. Bounded locally one-sided C1 graph regions have content-zero boundaries, and continuous-field integrals over their open diffeomorphic images equal integrals over their compact closures.

Boundary integration uses finite C1 graph charts, a subordinate smooth ambient partition, Gram area density, and the outward normal. The Riemann construction is choice-free; agreement with the stated Lebesgue construction additionally assumes Countable Choice.

The continuum balances are adopted smooth-model assumptions with positive density and temperature, no mass sources or relative diffusion, and no surface couples or intrinsic spin. Heat flux is positive outward; entropy flux uses local material temperature.

SI units distinguish model primitives from SI base quantities: density is kg m⁻³, velocity m s⁻¹, stress Pa, dynamic viscosity Pa s, and heat flux W m⁻². Primitive versus derived status is framework-local.

load_bearing.statement: Defines Newtonian spacetime and Cartesian inertial charts, rigid observer changes, C2 orientation-preserving material motions, Eulerian velocity and material derivative, velocity-gradient tensors, incompressibility, pathlines and streamlines, objective tensor transformation, tension-positive traction, and the SI quantity dictionary.

For every admissible bounded C1 material subregion, adopts reference-to-current mass conservation, linear and angular momentum balances with traction σn and no couples or intrinsic spin, total-energy balance with outward heat flux, and the entropy inequality with flux q/T at local material temperature. These are physical assumptions, not empirical findings or mathematical deductions.

For a bounded open locally one-sided C1 graph region V, a C1 diffeomorphism φ on a neighborhood of its closure, and continuous f on φ(U), V and φ(V) have locally C1 graph boundaries, their compact closures are Jordan measurable, their boundaries have content zero, and the integral of f over φ(V) equals its integral over φ(cl V).

A nonempty bounded open locally one-sided C1 graph region has compact boundary with finite graph charts and a subordinate nonnegative smooth ambient partition. The stated finite-chart Riemann integral of every continuous boundary field is finite and independent of charts and partition; the outward normal is continuous. Under Countable Choice these integrals agree with finite-chart Lebesgue surface integrals with the same Gram density.
For continuous h on an open Ω ⊆ R3, zero integrals over every bounded C1 subdomain compactly contained in Ω imply h = 0; nonnegative integrals over every such subdomain imply h ≥ 0.

Under the stated C2 orientation-preserving initial-normalized motion and positive C1 density, no-source material mass balance on every bounded C1 material subregion is equivalent to ∂tρ + div(ρu) = 0 and forces ρ(t,χ(t,a))J(t,a) = ρ0(a). For positive density, Dtρ = 0 throughout the material region if and only if div u = 0 there.

seams_checked.note: The draft smooth-motion, transport, and observer-calculus interfaces supply the asserted regularity, positive Jacobian, compact-Jordan transport, density invariance, and observer-spin formulas. Initial normalization is separately imposed locally; the open-region bridge is proved locally.

The turbulence remark uses compatible velocity, acceleration, and viscosity units and explicitly distinguishes pressure per unit mass from pressure in Pa. It makes no deduction of statistical closure from the continuum postulate.

The inspected mass, momentum, control-volume, and energy citations preserve material-region scope, traction sign, continuous-source regularity, and adopted-law status. Traction representation is acknowledged as already postulated.

Constitutive and thermodynamic closures are separately adopted. The cited strain, stress, SI, and continuum-balance conventions agree with their suppliers; constitutive coefficients are not inferred from balance laws.
The non-Newtonian definition preserves the material-motion, incompressibility, objective-tensor, stress, and SI conventions and separately declares its restricted closures and thermostat assumption.

Periodic and no-slip postulates use the supplier only for Cartesian, SI, gradient, and traction conventions. They explicitly adopt weak equations separately and interpret torus coordinates through local periodic lifts.

The observation postulate and filtering theorem cite absolute time, adapted Cartesian inertial coordinates, and Eulerian velocity in m s⁻¹ faithfully; their stochastic and apparatus assumptions are separate.

The geophysical postulate explicitly constructs a rotating adapted chart and relative velocity, preserving the distinction between inertial frames and rigid rotating observers. Reduced equations remain adopted approximations.

The phase-field postulate preserves Newtonian, SI, and tension-positive traction conventions. Its notes explicitly deny deriving the phase closure or a thermal completion from the supplier's total-energy and entropy balances.
